references.text: Jesus' self-identification as 'the light of the world' and his warning that whoever follows him will not walk in darkness but have the light of life, is a direct theological extension of the image in 11:10 where lack of light leads to stumbling.

The warning to walk while one has the light so that darkness does not overtake them, and the call to believe in the light, directly mirrors the logic in 11:10 that absence of light leads to stumbling.
Jesus' statement that he has come as a light into the world, so that no one who believes in him should remain in darkness, confirms the principle in 11:10 that light is necessary to avoid stumbling.

John writes that whoever walks in darkness does not know where they are going because darkness has blinded them, which is a direct parallel to 11:10 where whoever walks at night stumbles because the light is not in them.
The metaphor in Psalms of God's word as a lamp for the feet and a light for the path illustrates the same function that light has in 11:10: it is what prevents one from stumbling in darkness.
